# hook-master

> Local-first pointer registry and one-way materialization for agent hooks
> (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, Antigravity). Sibling to policy-registry, same
> pointer-only + optional-transport mechanic, applied to executable hook
> scripts instead of text policies.

Last-checked: 2026-09-10
Version: 0.2.0
Tests: 62 passed (pytest, tests/)
License: MIT
Repository: https://github.com/ellmos-ai/hook-master
Umbrella: https://github.com/open-bricks

## What this is

- A metadata-only registry (`~/.hook-master/registry.json`) of hook entries:
  `kind=hook` (a canonical script + SHA-256 hash + per-agent deploy targets)
  or `kind=consumer` (a registered external module that owns its own hook
  registration logic, e.g. memoryhooker/workflowhooker).
- A one-way materialization step (`deploy`/`diff`/`status`) that copies the
  canonical script to wherever each agent's own config expects it —
  canonical -> deployed, never the reverse.
- First-use consent allowlist (`~/.hook-master/allowlist.json`): fail-closed
  gate preventing unauthorized or unreviewed hook scripts from being materialized.
- Hook-Doctor diagnostics (`doctor [--id <id>] [--timing]`): checks hash match,
  `py_compile` syntax integrity, mtime drift, and agent config JSON/TOML validity.
- Fully standalone: works with zero network access and without
  system-gap-master installed. The optional `export-sync-view` command
  publishes a read-only metadata view into an existing `.SYNC/hooks/`
  layout if one exists, but nothing requires it.

## What this is NOT

- Not a replacement for memoryhooker/workflowhooker's own domain logic
  (checks, injectors, provider adapters) — those stay exactly where they
  are; hook-master only catalogues that they exist.
- Not a general event bus. It does not execute hooks, intercept events, or
  wrap an agent's own hook-invocation mechanism.
- Not an elevation layer. All hooks execute with the standard unprivileged
  credentials of the host agent process.

## Key files & directory structure

- `src/hook_master/model.py` — entry schema & validation.
- `src/hook_master/registry.py` — pointer store (register/get/search/verify).
- `src/hook_master/materialize.py` — deploy/diff/status materialization logic.
- `src/hook_master/consent.py` — HE2 first-use consent allowlist engine.
- `src/hook_master/doctor.py` — HE2 system & script health doctor.
- `src/hook_master/cli.py` — CLI entrypoint and argument routing.
- `src/hook_master/adapters/sync_hooks.py` — import/export bridge to
  `.SYNC/hooks/{adoption,registry}/<slot>.json`.
- `src/hook_master/adapters/system_gap.py` — optional system-gap-master seam.
- `library/` — canonical hook scripts this module carries.
- `tests/` — Pytest test suite covering model, registry, materialization, consent, doctor, metadata.

## CLI Usage Quick Reference

```bash
hook-master init                              # initialize registry
hook-master register <entry.json>             # register hook pointer
hook-master consent-status [<id>]             # show consent allowlist state
hook-master consent <id>                      # grant deploy consent
hook-master verify                            # verify canonical hashes
hook-master deploy [--dry-run]                # one-way copy canonical -> deploy_path
hook-master diff                              # inspect sync state / drift
hook-master status                            # verify + diff combined
hook-master doctor [--timing]                 # deep diagnostics & compile benchmarks
```
